First time in Osaka? Here's where we'd stay, and why 🏮

📍 Namba: Dotonbori is 3–5 min on foot, and the airport train stops here
🚆 Umeda: Kyoto in 29 min, Universal Studios about 15
🧸 Tennoji: calmer, the zoo is a short walk, 30 min from the airport

All three sit on one subway line, under 15 min apart.

🌃 Dotonbori: 3–5 min from Exit 14, best after dark

🔎 Private apartment? Check the listing shows a registration number

Want local Osaka, not the neon? Stay in Tenma 🏮

🛍️ Tenma: Japan's longest shopping street, 2.6 km under one roof, and Osaka Station is 1 stop on the JR Loop Line
🍶 Ura-Tenma: izakaya and standing-bar alleys about 5 min on foot from JR Tenma
🥩 Tsuruhashi: market lanes right outside the station, Kintetsu trains direct to Nara

Our take: 4+ nights or a second trip, go local. First trip with 2–3 nights, stay central.

Cup Noodles Museum in Osaka? Design your own cup for ¥500 🍜

🎨 My CUPNOODLES Factory: ¥500 per cup, no booking, numbered tickets on the day
👩‍🍳 Chicken Ramen Factory: 70 minutes of real cooking, book ahead (¥1,200 adults)
🏛️ The museum itself: free, with a tunnel of about 800 noodle packages

Our take: the ¥500 cup for most visits. No booking, and it fits easily into half a day.

Afterwards, walk up to Satsukiyama Park, where locals take their evening walks, for a free view over the whole Osaka plain 🌄 How to get there is in our bio 👆 or DM us NOODLES

Solo in Osaka on ¥5,000 a night? Book a weeknight 🛏️

On the Saturday we checked, the cheapest private room near Namba cost more than twice as much.

🥇 Weeknight: a single at Toho Hotel Namba Motomachi
• Its own toilet and shower: the cheapest fully private room we found that night.
• It came in just over budget, which is how Osaka stays cheap: move your Namba nights midweek.
• Finish the evening, walk back and close a door that's yours alone.

🥈 Saturday: a capsule at Asahi Plaza Shinsaibashi
• A bed, a locker and a shower, the cheapest bed close to the station that night.
• It's the move for a big night out: sleep close to where you finish.
• Several capsules are men-only or keep separate floors, so check before you book.

💡 Most people miss this: the cheapest single had its own shower room but a shared toilet. Read the facilities first if that matters.

Two minutes from the capsules there's a moss-covered statue people splash for luck. How to do it properly is waiting in our DMs: send PRIVACY 📩 (or tap the link in bio).

First night in Tokyo? Skip Shibuya Sky just for the crossing 🚦

From that high up the people are dots: it's a skyline ticket, not a crossing view.

🥇 Hachiko Square: free
• At peak times around 3,000 people cross on a single green, from every direction at once.
• Do it like a local: stand back from the kerb for one full light, then cross with the next wave.
• Halfway over, with everyone coming at you, is the moment you'll remember. Take your quick video there.

🥈 MAG8 rooftop at MAGNET by SHIBUYA109
• It sits right above the scramble and looks straight down onto it, a drink included in the entry.
• Go after dark: the crossing lit by the screens is the shot most people want, and there's an indoor lounge if it rains.
• Bring a card: it doesn't take cash.

💡 Most people miss this: the famous Starbucks window is standing room now, with the seats set back from the glass. Buy a drink for a look, not a seat.

Inside the station, a 30 m mural that was lost for decades sits beside free windows over the crossing. Its story is in our bio 👆 or DM us SCRAMBLE.

Two of you, one free afternoon in Osaka? Take the Hankyu line to Minoh Falls 🍁

On a weekday, an afternoon is enough: up to the falls and back at the station before dark.

🥇 The full walk to Minoh Falls
• A paved riverside path with no cars, climbing gently to a 33 m waterfall. Entry to the park is free.
• Go midweek: on leaf-season weekends the park office expects the path packed all the way from the station.
• Wear proper shoes, then just stand at the falls for a while before you walk down.

🥈 The short walk: Ryuan-ji and its red bridge
• Turn around at the temple and its red bridge, past the insect museum.
• The park office's own autumn photos were taken right here.
• All the colour on the lower path, none of the climb: the one for a late start or little legs.

💡 Most people miss this: shops on the first stretch of the path fry momiji tempura, Minoh's famous snack of salted maple leaves in sweet batter.

On the way back, get off one stop early: a family-run brewery pours its own beer at its taproom there 🍺 Where it is is in our bio 👆 or DM us MINOH.

First trip to Sapporo? Sleep in Odori ❄️

Sapporo's centre is small, and one straight underground walkway joins it all.

🥇 Odori, the middle of everything
• It sits right beside Odori Park, with the TV Tower at the park's east end. Sapporo Station is a short underground walk away, and Susukino is one subway stop.
• The Chi-Ka-Ho walkway runs underground between Sapporo Station and Odori, so you can get around even in a blizzard. It's the reason Odori works so well in winter.
• Breakfast is a seafood bowl at Nijo Market, close to Odori Station. For another market, the Tozai Line runs four stops to the Curb Market.

🥈 Susukino, if dinner is the point
• This is Sapporo's night district, and the place for jingisukan, grilled mutton.
• Daruma's main branch, near Susukino Station, grills it every night of the week.
• The streets stay busy until late, so light sleepers should ask for a high floor or stay a few blocks away.

💡 Most people miss this: Sapporo's tourism office says pavements freeze in deep winter. Pack boots with grip; convenience stores sell anti-slip spikes.

There's also a corner of Susukino Market where rice balls are made by hand, in the style the tourism office recommends 🍙 It's in our bio 👆 or DM us SAPPORO.

A few days in Kyoto? Sleep where the train lines cross 🚃

Kyoto's own tourism office warns that city buses like the 205 and 206 get very crowded in season, and recommends trains and the subway.

🥇 Shijo-Karasuma, our pick
• The Karasuma subway line (north–south) and the Hankyu line (east–west) cross right here, so you can head off in every direction.
• Kyoto Station is one short subway ride away and Kawaramachi is one Hankyu stop. Arashiyama is on the Hankyu line too, with one change at Katsura.
• It's Kyoto's business district: office blocks, not wooden houses. The old-Kyoto atmosphere starts a short walk east.

🥈 Kawaramachi / Gion, for evenings
• Walk out at dusk to Yasaka-jinja and the lanes of Gion, with Nishiki Market next door.
• The market association asks visitors to eat in front of the shop rather than while walking.
• Lodging here is mostly long-standing ryokan and luxury hotels, so there are fewer budget rooms.

💡 Most people miss this: the Subway & Bus 1-Day Pass covers only the calendar day you start it, not 24 hours.

Quiet mornings near Shibuya? Don't move out, stay on the park side 🌳

The "quiet" neighbours look close, but on the rail map neither Yoyogi-Hachiman nor Yoyogi-Uehara is one stop from Shibuya, and both need a change of train every night.

🥇 Central Shibuya, north side toward Yoyogi Park
• You walk home from dinner: no last train, no change, no fare, no watching the clock.
• Over three nights, that saves about an hour and a half of evening trains.
• Some hotels on this side are under 1 km from Yoyogi Park, so a morning walk is still easy.

🥈 Yoyogi-Hachiman, for early risers
• A small Odakyu Line station on the west side of Yoyogi Park.
• The park is always open and free, so a walk at dawn is easy.
• The catch: coming home from Shibuya means changing trains at Shimokitazawa, every night.

💡 Most people miss this: Yoyogi-Uehara has very few hotels. It's mostly apartments, so it suits a stay of a week or more.

A few minutes from Yoyogi-Uehara stands Japan's largest mosque, one of the most beautiful interiors in Tokyo, and visitors are welcome for free 🕌 How to visit respectfully is in our DMs: send YOYOGI.

Big suitcase into Sapporo? Take the airport train ✈️🚆

🥇 The JR Rapid Airport train

• Its station is directly under New Chitose's Domestic Terminal, so you just follow the signs down from arrivals to the platform.

• With Suica, ICOCA, PASMO or Kitaca you just tap through and take any non-reserved car, no ticket queue. Without one, the ticket machines take cash only, while the orange reserved-seat machines and the JR counter take cards.

• Luggage is limited to two items each, which suits most trips. More big bags than that? Look at the bus or a pre-booked transfer instead.

🥈 The airport bus, if your hotel is a stop

• Hokuto Kotsu's buses stop at Sapporo Station, Susukino and several big Odori hotels, so you can skip the station entirely and step off at your door.

• No reservation needed: you pay as you get off, by cash, contactless card or PayPay. Suica doesn't work on it.

• It's one suitcase per person in the hold, and since there are no reservations, a full bus means waiting for the next one.

💡 At busy times, car 4 is the reserved u-seat car: a guaranteed seat and space for a big case. You can book it ahead online as a ticketless reservation.

Before you even head down to the trains, a Hakodate seafood bowl from a shop that began at Hakodate's morning market is waiting in the terminal 🍣 DM us CHITOSE and we'll send you where.

Skip midday at Tokyo's Senso-ji. Come early, or after dinner 🏮

🥇 Early morning, before breakfast
• The grounds never close, so you can walk through Kaminarimon and down Nakamise before a single stall has opened.
• Come early if you want to step inside the main hall without the crowds. It's the one thing an evening visit can't give you.
• Then walk to MISOJYU, a miso soup shop nearby, for its morning set: miso soup, a rice ball, half a seasoned egg and pickles. A warm, quiet start before Asakusa wakes up.

🥈 After dinner, lit up
• Kaminarimon, Hozomon, the five-storied pagoda and the main hall are lit every evening, and the paths are quieter than at midday.
• Walk Nakamise once the shops have closed: the stall shutters are painted, so the street turns into a gallery you never see by day.
• The hall itself is shut at night, so this visit is for photos and a slow walk. Staying in Asakusa? You can do both quiet visits in one day.

💡 For the view straight down Nakamise, go up to the free 8th-floor terrace of the Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center, right opposite Kaminarimon.

A short walk away, one of only four Tokyo theatres with rakugo every day of the year lets you drift in between acts 🎭 It's in our bio, or DM us SENSOJI.

Going to Sapporo before Christmas? ✨❄️
Two winter events, both around Odori Park.

🥇 Munich Christmas Market
📅 20 Nov to 25 Dec 2026
🍷 Hot wine, hot chocolate and Sapporo beer.
☕ The mug has a new design every year.
🥨 Sausages, pretzels and roasted almonds.
🤝 Sapporo and Munich are sister cities.

🥈 Sapporo White Illumination
📅 Odori Park, until 25 Dec 2026
💡 This is its 46th year.
🌳 Minami 1-jo street: about 70,000 lights
on 46 ginkgo trees.
✨ New this year: the old Red Brick Office,
lit in blue.
❄️ Some lights stay on into Feb and Mar 2027.

💡 Our tip
Eat at the market huts first.
Then walk the lights after the stalls close.
The crowds are smaller by then.

Christmas markets in Tokyo: free or paid? 🎄
Here's one of each for December 2026.

🥇 Roppongi Hills · free
📅 21 Nov to 25 Dec 2026
✨ Its 20th year, with about ten stalls.
🎁 German ornaments from Käthe Wohlfahrt.
🥨 Hot wine, sausages and fresh pretzels.
💙 After dark, walk Keyakizaka's blue lights.

🥈 Yokohama Red Brick Warehouse · paid
📅 20 Nov to 25 Dec 2026
🎄 An 11 m live tree and a roof of lights.
🍷 German huts and a new mug every year.
🌃 The harbour and skyline right behind it.
🎟️ Entry from ¥500, part of it is free.

💡 Good to know
The Tokyo Christmas Market moved again.
It's at Shin-Toyosu by the water,
and in Shiba Park from 4 Dec.

Ring a temple bell yourself in Kyoto 🔔
New Year's Eve, 31 Dec 2026.

🔔 Temples strike their bells 108 times
to clear away the year's worldly desires.

🥇 Shinnyo-do · ring it
📅 31 Dec, from 23:45
👥 Four or five people strike it together.
🎫 No ticket needed.
🍵 Free herbal tea while it lasts.

🥈 Chion-in · watch it
📅 31 Dec, from 22:20
🙏 17 monks swing a 4 m log
at a bell of about 70 tonnes.
📝 Watching is by advance application only.
👀 Its trial ringing on 27 Dec is free to watch.

🌇 Early night? Myoman-ji
📅 31 Dec, 15:00 to 17:00
🔔 Ring out the year, then go to dinner.

Tokyo has a free city view, 202 m up 🌇
It's in Shinjuku. Two hours before dinner?
See the garden first.

🍁 The maples turn red in late autumn.
🌳 Stay near the Shinjuku Gate end.
⏰ In winter it closes early, so go first.

🥈 Tokyo government building
🏙️ The observatory is free, 202 m up.
🌅 Go near sunset, stay for the lights.
✨ After dark, a free light show
plays on the building's outside wall.

⛩️ Behind Golden Gai, red gates lead
to a quiet shrine where performers pray for luck.

Kansai Airport to Kyoto: visitors pay less 🚆
The Haruka has a ticket only for visitors.

🥇 JR Haruka · most arrivals

⏱️ About 75–80 minutes, no change.

🎫 Visitor one-way ticket: ¥2,700.

🛂 For foreign passports on a visitor stay.

🥈 Limousine bus · late flights

🌙 It runs over an hour after the last Haruka.

🧳 Your suitcases ride in the hold.

🚏 It stops on Kyoto Station's south side.

🥉 Trains via Osaka · travelling light

💴 Cheapest, about ¥1,670.

🔁 But you change trains with your bags.

Save this before your Fuji day.

1️⃣ Highway bus from Busta Shinjuku

⏱️ About 1 h 45, depending on traffic.

🎫 ¥2,000 booked online.

🧳 One big case each rides free in the hold.

⏱️ About 2 hours, direct, no traffic.

🎫 ¥4,200; seats go on sale a month ahead.

🌅 Direct trains leave Tokyo only in the morning.

✅ One case each? Take the bus.
